memory_leads.lead: Health-related labor availability is a role-and-readiness chain linking the seafarer, master or designated shipboard medical-responsible personnel, owner/operator or shipmanager, shore medical/telemedical support, port or emergency services and later repatriation/return-to-work support. A person can remain employed and certificated while temporarily unavailable for assigned duties.

Medical fitness is an eligibility/readiness state separate from professional certification. The operationally relevant distinction is whether a person is presently fit, restricted, under review or unavailable for the intended duties; exact medical criteria and decisions require Evidence and professional authority.

Occupational-health risk accumulates through working-environment exposures and task design rather than only through sudden accidents. Noise, vibration, heat/cold, chemicals, repetitive or manual work, disrupted sleep and prolonged isolation are remembered as broad exposure families, but exact dose or health effect is not established here.

Illness or injury recognition creates a time-sensitive operational state before diagnosis is complete. The ship may need to redistribute tasks, increase monitoring or seek shore advice while cause, severity and expected duration remain uncertain; replay should preserve that uncertainty rather than backfill later medical findings.

Onboard medical response is constrained by trained personnel, carried resources, communications, distance from shore and the patient's ability to continue duties. Structurally, the decision space includes onboard support, consultation, shore referral and evacuation, but Memory must not prescribe treatment.

Telemedical or shore medical consultation is an information bridge between limited onboard observation and external expertise. Advice quality and operational usefulness depend on what symptoms, measurements, history and communications can be transmitted; exact providers, protocols and medical advice require Evidence.

Shore referral is a logistics state as well as a medical state. Port accessibility, immigration or entry arrangements, local medical capability, vessel schedule and transport can determine whether a recommended evaluation is operationally feasible without implying any particular medical threshold.

Medical evacuation can remove a critical role abruptly and may require route deviation, rendezvous, port call or external rescue coordination. The capacity effect depends on the affected person's duties, remaining watch coverage and replacement timing, not simply on the number of people onboard.

Mental-health strain is an occupational-readiness dimension that can interact with isolation, fatigue, prolonged tours, family separation, workload and workplace climate. Memory can retain the existence of a support/readiness state without diagnosing individuals or inferring causation from later events.

Infectious or communicable illness can create crew-level rather than individual availability effects when multiple people require isolation, monitoring or shore restrictions. Exact disease, quarantine, testing or public-health rules are date- and jurisdiction-specific and remain Evidence work.

Recovery, repatriation and return-to-work are separate states. Discharge from acute care does not automatically mean fit for original duties, and a worker may need recovery, reassessment, restricted duties or replacement planning before normal deployment resumes; exact medical decisions require professional Evidence.

A health-related absence can propagate through a tightly staffed watch system: task redistribution raises workload on remaining crew, which can reduce rest opportunity and increase relief urgency even when statutory or nominal manning headcount has not yet changed.

Health events affect retention and career continuity as well as one voyage. Recurrent injury, chronic limitation, prolonged recovery or perceived weakness of onboard/welfare support can influence whether experienced personnel return to sea, adding another attrition channel to the P035 survivor pipeline without establishing any individual medical outcome.

P033 employment/welfare is refined because medical care and repatriation are not a single support event: health status, duty availability, shore access, travel, employer coordination and later return-to-work can follow different timelines.

P032 fatigue and workload are refined by health-related task redistribution. An apparently adequate crew can become functionally thin when one skilled person is medically unavailable and remaining watches absorb the work.

P035 formal qualification is refined by medical readiness: certificate validity and rank competence do not imply current deployability if health status restricts the intended duties, so usable labor is the intersection of qualification, assignment and health-readiness states.

Known-time replay should separate first symptom/injury report, initial onboard assessment, external consultation, shore or evacuation decision, later diagnosis, recovery status and eventual return-to-duty. Later clinical clarity must not overwrite the earlier operational uncertainty.
P033 already identified illness/injury care and repatriation as employment-lifecycle states; P036 decomposes the occupational-health readiness chain instead of repeating that support category.
P032 already covers fatigue and P029 emergency response broadly; P036 applies those interfaces specifically to health-related availability without changing their established semantics.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Clinical criteria, diagnosis and treatment require authoritative medical Evidence and qualified professional judgment; blind Memory must not provide medical advice.
Individual health facts, causation and exposure limits require claim-scoped medical, occupational-health or investigation Evidence.
Provider capability, coverage and historical lineages would become a directory and require source-first verification.
Current health and public-health conditions are source-first claims and outside blind-current authority.

stop_reason: The occupational-health readiness chain is populated from fitness and broad exposure/prevention through illness/injury recognition, onboard support, external consultation, shore referral/evacuation, recovery/repatriation and return-to-duty. Further recall becomes diagnosis-, treatment-, drug-, medical-standard-, injury-, mental-health-case-, provider-, medevac- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not medical advice; no diagnosis, treatment, drug recommendation, medical-fitness determination, exposure-health causation, mental-health assessment, evacuation necessity, provider capability or current crew-health condition is verified.
